# anypoint_private_space_transit_gateway (Resource)

Manages an AWS Transit Gateway attachment on an Anypoint CloudHub 2.0 private space. Two modes: create mode (`name`, `resource_share_id`, `resource_share_account`) creates the transit gateway connection from a RAM resource share owned by your AWS account, with the MuleSoft AWS account whitelisted as principal and the TGW associated with the share; attach mode (`transit_gateway_id`) attaches an existing organization transit gateway, for example the one created by another resource, to this private space. Deleting the resource only detaches the private space. The organization-level transit gateway stays listed after its last attachment is removed. Re-attaching a private space shortly after a detach can take several minutes; the provider retries for up to 15 minutes. Create mode re-attaches an organization transit gateway left by an earlier detach when no other private space uses it. Two create-mode resources on one resource share are an error: give the second one `transit_gateway_id` instead. Replacing a create-mode resource replaces the attach-mode resources that reference its `transit_gateway_id`. `create_before_destroy` on create-mode resources across private spaces is not supported; use attach mode. An existing create-mode resource moves to attach mode without replacement: set `transit_gateway_id` to its current value and remove `name`, `resource_share_id` and `resource_share_account`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Attach an AWS Transit Gateway to an Anypoint CloudHub 2.0 private space.
#
# Prereqs (AWS side):
#   1. An aws_ec2_transit_gateway in the same region as the private space.
#   2. An aws_ram_resource_share with allow_external_principals = true.
#   3. The MuleSoft AWS account whitelisted as principal on that share.
#   4. The transit gateway associated to the share.
#
# Use the anypoint_private_space_mulesoft_account data source to discover the
# MuleSoft AWS account id for the target private space — it is region-bound,
# so do NOT hardcode it.

data "anypoint_private_space_mulesoft_account" "this" {
  org_id           = var.root_org
  private_space_id = var.private_space_id
}

resource "aws_ec2_transit_gateway" "this" {
  description                    = "anypoint-tgw"
  amazon_side_asn                = 64512
  auto_accept_shared_attachments = "enable"

  tags = {
    Name = "anypoint-tgw"
  }
}

resource "aws_ram_resource_share" "this" {
  name                      = "anypoint-tgw-share"
  allow_external_principals = true
}

resource "aws_ram_principal_association" "mulesoft" {
  principal          = data.anypoint_private_space_mulesoft_account.this.account_id
  resource_share_arn = aws_ram_resource_share.this.arn
}

resource "aws_ram_resource_association" "tgw" {
  resource_arn       = aws_ec2_transit_gateway.this.arn
  resource_share_arn = aws_ram_resource_share.this.arn
}

data "aws_caller_identity" "current" {}

# Create mode: creates the transit gateway connection from the RAM share and
# attaches it to the first private space.
resource "anypoint_private_space_transit_gateway" "a" {
  org_id           = var.root_org
  private_space_id = var.private_space_id
  name             = "my-tgw"

  # Trailing UUID of the RAM share ARN (NOT the full ARN).
  resource_share_id = element(
    split("/", aws_ram_resource_share.this.arn),
    length(split("/", aws_ram_resource_share.this.arn)) - 1,
  )
  resource_share_account = data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id

  # Static routes pushed into the private space route table.
  # Must NOT equal or be more specific than the private space CIDR.
  routes = ["10.4.0.0/18"]

  depends_on = [
    aws_ram_resource_association.tgw,
    aws_ram_principal_association.mulesoft,
  ]
}

# Attach mode: attaches the same transit gateway to a second private space in
# the same organization and region. The reference orders the creates. The
# name belongs to resource "a"; name and resource_share_* are not set here.
resource "anypoint_private_space_transit_gateway" "b" {
  org_id             = var.root_org
  private_space_id   = var.private_space_id_b
  transit_gateway_id = anypoint_private_space_transit_gateway.a.transit_gateway_id

  routes = ["10.4.0.0/18"]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `org_id` (String) The organization id where the private space lives.
- `private_space_id` (String) The private space id.
- `routes` (Set of String) Static routes (CIDR strings) pushed into the private space route table. Must not equal or be more specific than the private space CIDR.

### Optional

- `last_updated` (String) The last time this resource has been updated locally.
- `name` (String) Display name of the transit gateway attachment. Create mode only: in attach mode the name belongs to the resource that created the transit gateway and is read back.
- `resource_share_account` (String) AWS account id that owns the RAM share (your AWS account, NOT MuleSoft's). Create mode only.
- `resource_share_id` (String) RAM resource share UUID (trailing GUID of the ARN, NOT the full ARN). Create mode only; requires `resource_share_account` and `name`.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `transit_gateway_id` (String) The AWS transit gateway id (e.g. tgw-...). Set it to attach an existing organization transit gateway (for example another resource's `transit_gateway_id`) to this private space; leave it unset to create the transit gateway connection from a RAM resource share.

### Read-Only

- `account_id` (String) MuleSoft AWS account id, region-bound to the private space.
- `id` (String) Composite id ORG_ID/PRIVATE_SPACE_ID/TRANSIT_GATEWAY_ID.
- `region` (String) AWS region (inherits the private space region).
- `space_name` (String) Private space display name.
- `status_attachment` (String) Attachment status (refreshing, available, ...).
- `status_gateway` (String) Gateway status (refreshing, available, ...).
- `tgw_resource_url` (String) AWS console URL of the transit gateway.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# In order for the import to work, you should provide a ID composed of the following:
#  {ORG_ID}/{PRIVATE_SPACE_ID}/{TRANSIT_GATEWAY_ID}

terraform import \
  -var-file params.tfvars.json \
  anypoint_private_space_transit_gateway.my_tgw \
  aa1f55d6-213d-4f60-845c-201282484cd1/7f747999-a9bb-41d5-bfe8-d6b8cca68c62/tgw-017e20b9ce00c865c
```
